name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd

ledger.quote: Our disbursal guidance for FY26 remains in the range of Rs. 5,600-5,800 Cr.
ledger.speaker: Manoj Viswanathan
ledger.verdict: FY26 disbursement guidance of Rs 5,600-5,800 Cr was not specifically confirmed on the call.

ledger.quote: We intend to add 6 new branches in Q2.
ledger.speaker: Manoj Viswanathan
ledger.verdict: Branch addition target of six branches in Q2 FY26 was not updated in the call.

ledger.quote: We continue to maintain a credit cost guidance of 30 to 40 bps, ensuring disciplined risk management even as we scale.
ledger.speaker: Manoj Viswanathan
ledger.verdict: Credit cost guidance of 30-40 bps for FY26 was not updated in the latest call.

ledger.quote: We expect this ratio to remain range bound within 2.6% - 2.7% as we focus on growth and expansion.
ledger.speaker: Nutan Gaba Patwari
ledger.verdict: Q1 FY27 opex to assets was 2.8%, with guidance maintained at 2.6%-2.7%.
ledger.evidence: Reported operating cost to assets was 2.8%. As we continue to invest for growth, we expect this ratio to broadly remain range bound within 2.6%, 2.7%.

ledger.quote: We aim to take co-lending contribution to 10% of disbursements as we scale.
ledger.speaker: Nutan Gaba Patwari
ledger.verdict: Co-lending disbursements were Rs 46 crore (2.8% of disbursements) against 10% target.
ledger.evidence: Co-lending disbursements were INR46 crore, taking co-lending book to INR617 crore, 3.6% of the AUM. We remain focused on scaling this channel by strengthening the enabling infrastructure.

ledger.quote: We aim to deliver 15% ROE in the next five to six quarters and then build from there.
ledger.speaker: Nutan Gaba Patwari
ledger.verdict: Return on equity reached 14.5% in Q1 FY27, approaching the 15% target.
ledger.evidence: Return on Assets improved by 10 basis points sequentially to 4.2%, while Return on Equity improved by 50 basis points to 14.5%.

ledger.quote: We plan to add four to five new branches in the upcoming quarter.
ledger.speaker: Manoj Viswanathan
ledger.verdict: Branch addition target of 4 to 5 branches in Q3 FY26 was not reported.

ledger.quote: We are aiming to get it under 8%, let us say, by March.
ledger.speaker: Nutan Gaba Patwari
ledger.verdict: Cost of borrowing was reduced to 7.8% in Q1 FY27, meeting sub-8% target.
ledger.evidence: On the liability side, proactive management of our borrowing mix led to a further 10 basis point sequential reduction, bringing cost of borrowing down to 7.8%.

ledger.quote: We have 6-8 branches in the pipeline and at least 6 branches will be added in Q4.
ledger.speaker: Manoj Viswanathan
ledger.target: Add at least 6 branches in Q4
ledger.verdict: Target of adding at least six branches in Q4 FY26 was not reported.

ledger.quote: As we move toward FY27, we are positioned to achieve 25% AUM growth driven by enhanced distribution
ledger.speaker: Manoj Viswanathan
ledger.verdict: AUM grew 25.7% year-on-year to Rs 16,938 crore in Q1 FY27, meeting 25% target.
ledger.evidence: AUM stood at INR16,938 crore as of Jun'26, growing 25.7% year-on-year and 6.7% sequentially.

ledger.quote: We aim to take co-lending contribution to 10% of AUM as we scale.
ledger.speaker: Nutan Gaba Patwari
ledger.verdict: Co-lending book reached Rs 617 crore, representing 3.6% of AUM against 10% target.
ledger.evidence: Co-lending disbursements were INR46 crore, taking co-lending book to INR617 crore, 3.6% of the AUM. We remain focused on scaling this channel by strengthening the enabling infrastructure.

ledger.quote: FY27, again, we are looking to add about 25-30 branches.
ledger.speaker: Manoj Viswanathan
ledger.verdict: Added four branches in Q1 FY27 towards the full-year target of 25-30 branches.
ledger.evidence: during the quarter, we added four branches, one each in Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Madhya Pradesh, taking our network to 175 branches and 373 touch points.

ledger.quote: That will be in the region of around 20%-23% AUM growth Y-o-Y if we have to get to Rs. 35,000 crores.
ledger.speaker: Manoj Viswanathan
ledger.verdict: AUM reached Rs 16,938 crore in Q1 FY27, growing 25.7% YoY towards 2030 target.
ledger.evidence: AUM stood at INR16,938 crore as of Jun'26, growing 25.7% year-on-year and 6.7% sequentially.

ledger.quote: Our aim remains to deliver a spread at a portfolio level in our guided range of 5% to 5.25%.
ledger.speaker: Nutan Gaba Patwari
ledger.verdict: Spread excluding co-lending reached 5.3% in Q1 FY27, within guided range.
ledger.evidence: Incremental borrowing cost during the quarter remained favourable at 7.6%. Consequently, spread, excluding co-lending, remained healthy at 5.3%.

ledger.quote: Guidance on the credit cost is the same.  30bps to 40bps.
ledger.speaker: Manoj Viswanathan
ledger.verdict: Credit cost for Q1 FY27 was 40 bps, within guided 30-40 bps range.
ledger.evidence: Credit cost for Q1 was 40 basis points. Provision coverage on Stage 3 assets was 23.4% as of Jun'26 compared to 23.9% in Q4FY26.

open.quote: We remain confident of delivering 25% AUM growth while maintaining our focus on profitability, portfolio quality and operating efficiency.
open.speaker: Manoj Viswanathan

open.quote: As we continue to invest for growth, we expect this ratio to broadly remain range bound within 2.6%, 2.7%.
open.speaker: Nutan Patwari

read: Management consistently delivers on core financial parameters, successfully maintaining credit costs at 40 bps, spreads at 5.3%, and sub-8% borrowing costs. However, quarterly branch addition targets and historic FY26 operational milestones are rarely closed out explicitly on calls.
questions: Why did operating cost to assets rise to 2.8% in Q1 FY27 against the guided 2.6%-2.7% range?
What concrete measures are being taken to scale co-lending contribution from 3.6% to 10% of AUM?
bull: AUM grew 25.7% year-on-year to Rs 16,938 crore in Q1 FY27.
Cost of borrowing reduced to 7.8%, driving spreads to 5.3% in Q1 FY27.
Q1 FY27 PAT increased by 34.5% year-on-year to Rs 160 crore.
bear: Operating cost to assets rose to 2.8% in Q1 FY27, above 2.6%-2.7% guidance.
Co-lending contribution remains low at 3.6% of AUM versus 10% target.
